name: Fixed-Test Criterion for Universal Substitution
statement: For a nonempty proper test $T\subsetneq Q^Y$, universality is equivalent to the existence, on $Y$ plus auxiliaries and with one common mark, of maximum classes $L,N_0,N_1,U$ of ranks $s-1,s,s,s+1$ satisfying $L\subseteq N_0,N_1\subseteq U$ and marked sections $\varnothing,T,T^{\mathrm c},Q^Y$. A rank-$R$ parent of $H_T$ supplies these with $s=R-1$. Given this interval and a proper rank-$r$ parent of the outer class with $m$ auxiliaries, substitution has a rank-$(r+s)$ parent with the old auxiliaries plus those of the interval.
proof: Projecting and fully reducing a parent of the three-section class in its two controls extracts the four consecutive maximum classes and their marked sections. Conversely, extend one nested side of the interval and the projection/reduction pair of the outer parent to maximum sequences. A level sum followed by componentwise replacement of the middle fiber by $N_0$ or $N_1$ gives the required maximum parent and retains both marks.
